purpose: Define the logical order of a 5-8 image ecommerce product suite.
principle: Each image answers one buyer question. The suite progresses from click stop, to interest, to proof, to use imagination, to conversion support.

slots.buyer_question: What is this and why should I stop scrolling?
What problem does it solve for me?
slots.risk: model may invent claims if ProductTruthPack is weak

slots.buyer_question: Is the product real, durable, and trustworthy?
slots.copy_policy: proof labels, material/part callouts, no unsupported specs
slots.risk: detail panels may hallucinate product internals

slots.buyer_question: Where will I use it and what does ownership feel like?
slots.copy_policy: little or no text; reserve overlay zone
slots.risk: scene generation can alter product identity

slots.buyer_question: Why this instead of the alternative?
slots.copy_policy: truthful comparison only; no fake performance claims
slots.risk: before/after can become legally or factually risky

slots.buyer_question: What is included and what reduces purchase risk?
slots.copy_policy: included items, warranty, package quantity, compatibility
slots.risk: quantity/warranty must come from listing or manufacturer source

slots.buyer_question: Can I quickly scan all major benefits?
slots.risk: model text and icons are usually not production safe

slots.buyer_question: Can the marketplace algorithm clearly identify the SKU?
slots.risk: boring but useful for platform recognition

suite_consistency_rules: Use one design system per suite.
Use one accent palette across all slots.
Repeat product scale logic, badge shape, shadow direction, and typography.
Do not repeat the same selling point in every image.
Keep exact product facts in ProductTruthPack and forbidden claims in every prompt.
